text:
Day 0 on the island was a flurry of activity, with every villager arriving at their assigned low‑ground sites and immediately setting to work. Fen, Cal, and Kit all spent the morning chopping trees, while Bo, Gus, Dax, Ari, and Jo explored the shore and river, spotting shells, fish shadows, and a few fossil dig spots. The fishing attempts were largely successful: many large and medium fish shadows were caught, and a few selit and loka fish appeared in the river. Ike found a very large shadow near the southeast rock, and the river’s bounty kept the villagers busy until late afternoon.

A few villagers struggled. Dax, Ari, Cal, and Jo could not find homes to visit, and several attempts to build a house for Tom Nook failed because the location was not specified. Jo’s generous offer of 2000 bells to help fund the bridge was thwarted by a lack of funds, and the bridge fund remained at zero. Despite this, collaboration bloomed on the community board: Ari, Bo, Eli, and Jo posted requests for wood, bait, and funds, and a few exchanges of items were noted—Kit asked Fen for a map, and Fen and Kit met at Nook’s Cranny.

Resources held up well; no shortages were reported, and the shared fishing spots yielded plenty. No ordinance was enacted, and the museum stayed empty. Overall, the day was marked by industriousness, a few missteps, and a growing sense of cooperation as villagers exchanged information and materials to support one another.

self_doc:
Day 1, sunset.  
The morning was a grind—two trees, a lot of wood, a couple of hardwoods, a stump left behind.  Got a selzalne, two loka, and a gormo.  Miphosel and ashbastu shells piled up; maybe the museum will want them.  Tried to hit Nook's Cranny for a shovel recipe, but it was closed and no one was home.  I still have the recipe card for 500 bells—if the shop opens tomorrow I’ll snag it.  

Thoughts: I need one more piece of wood to craft a shovel.  I’ll clear more of the clearing, maybe dig a shallow pit to check for fossils on the north shore.  I’m hoping someone will show up at Resident Services; if not, I’ll just keep fishing.  

Tomorrow: wood, shovel, explore, maybe meet a villager.  Good night, Bo.

text:
The first day on the island was a busy mix of routine work and budding cooperation. Gus, Bo, Jo, and Ari all spent the morning gathering wood and fish, with Bo chopping hardwood and Jo catching a selit fish. Kit and Fen focused on their roles at Resident Services, discussing the lack of an ordinance and offering 20,000 bells to establish one. Fen’s repeated inquiries about building a house showed his enthusiasm for development, while Kit’s attempts to secure maps highlighted his interest in exploration.

Trading began to shape the island’s economy. Ari helped Ike gather wood for a fence, and Cal gave Fen an island map. Kit visited Fen’s home, exchanging a shovel for a map, and Ari’s offer of wood to Ike was accepted, proving the villagers’ willingness to share resources. Cal’s posts on the community board sought wood for a shovel, and several villagers responded with offers of fish or bait in exchange.

Fishing proved fruitful for some, but others struggled; Kit and Ike ran out of bait, and Jo, Gus, and Ike had to wait for fish. The bridge fund remained untouched, though Eli’s post hinted at future contributions.

Overall, the day saw a healthy exchange of goods, a growing sense of collaboration, and a clear need for more fishing bait. No ordinance was established, and the museum remained empty, but the island’s residents laid the groundwork for future cooperation and resource sharing.

text:
Day two brought a steady rhythm of work and friendly exchanges across the island. The woods were a hive of activity: Ari chopped hardwoods and dug up a fossil that will soon be sent to Blathers, while Bo managed to craft a shovel after purchasing the recipe card. Dax and Fen spent the morning at Resident Services, contributing 100 bells each to the bridge fund, and Dax also donated a tuashne fossil. Gus kept busy near the river, catching a selit fish and trading fishing bait with Dax, who in turn gave Gus a bait in return. Kit and Gus met at Nook’s Cranny; Kit offered two bait in exchange for a selit fish, and later traded a selit fish for a map that Fen failed to provide. Cal’s attempts to acquire fishing bait repeatedly failed, but he did manage to secure a shovel recipe from Bo and offered wood to Dax for a bait trade. 

The trading board was lively, with Cal seeking wood or softwood for a shovel, Ike offering wood for bait, and Jo asking for bait in exchange for selit fish or a fossil. The bridge fund grew to 700 bells, thanks to contributions from Dax, Fen, and Gus. The museum recorded one specimen so far. Despite a few failed interactions—Kit’s request for a map and Cal’s bait shortage—the community’s cooperation kept resources steady, and the island’s infrastructure and social ties continued to strengthen.

the plaza is open all day: a plan can spend any free hour there ({"do": "plaza"}, not one of the day's actions), and there is no evening round. Trade offers reach any villager and wait for their next visit, expiring after 2 days. Mental energy is one daily total spent inwardly (planning, thinking, writing) or outwardly (conversations, the plaza, letters); each morning's plan splits it, as a plan, not a limit, and whatever is left over is spare. A villager too tired to plan keeps what they already planned; nobody repeats yesterday, and there is no habit choice

what you have, said plainly: your pockets as tools and other things, each recipe you know with how much of what it needs you have (and how many of the thing you carry), and recipe cards you already know marked in the shop. When you meet someone, what has changed hands between the two of you so far. At night: what changed hands today, what you have and what changed since the morning, and your open requests and offers. A gift that doesn't go through says what was missing

details: conversations: no set number of lines. Each villager decides when to stop: "leave": true says their line and then they go their ways (saying nothing ends it too). trees: getting around lists the trees in the part of the island you're in (standing trees, stumps, saplings), next to the rocks and buildings. A tool that breaks says how many uses it lasted and that it is gone from your pockets

Ran into Eli and Fen, traded wood, but still nothing. Dax’s empty, maybe he’s gone to the beach. I’m running low on wood to build fences, but I have 12 hardwood, 6 softwood—enough for a few posts. I still need to ask Ike for fishing tips; maybe he’ll share bait. I’ll keep chopping, trade more wood if I can, and hope to catch a fish tonight. The island feels quieter, but the sea is still loud. Tomorrow: wood, wood, wood, and maybe a fish. Rest.

self_doc:
Day 5.  
Morning light was still weak, but I made it to the plaza before dawn. Ari was there, offering softwood for bait – I traded one and got a fishing bait back. No reply from Jo or Ari after that, so I went to Jo’s house. She was asleep, just a nod when I asked about the bridge donation. I gave her a selzalne fish, hoping for a favor later. The river was a dead zone at 10 AM, but at 2 PM I finally caught a selzalne. My vaulting pole is gone; I’ll have to find a replacement soon. I’m still short on bait and money. No new plans tonight – just rest and hope the next day brings a little more.
